claims.statement: East-node carrier feed or dock infrastructure has a lag or defect independent of allocation, affecting only orders routed there by v18.
claims.corroboration: m8_r_dock confirms east-node dock capacity is normal with no queueing. This rules out warehouse-side saturation or infrastructure defect as root cause.
claims.limitation: Disproven by direct dock capacity observation. Independent east-node infrastructure issue is ruled out.

claims.statement: Allocation rule set v18 creates split-reservation format that is incompatible with carrier protocol or pickup systems; carriers cannot or will not process split-reservation orders, causing the hold.
claims.corroboration: m8_r_exceptions shows 100% of held orders are v18-allocated split-reservation; m8_r_dock shows dock is normal (ruling out warehouse saturation); m8_e03 shows v18 introduced split-reservation pattern. Convergence of evidence: v18 is the cause, split-reservation format is the mechanism, carrier incompatibility is the trigger.
claims.limitation: Carrier-side protocol incompatibility is inferred from dock normality and 100% v18 correlation, not from direct carrier rejection notice. However, no other explanation remains viable.

resolutions.rationale: Dock capacity check (m8_r_dock) shows east-node dock is normal with no queue, eliminating dock saturation hypothesis. This leaves only v18 split-reservation format incompatibility as viable root cause. Regression suite was green because it did not test split-reservation carrier-protocol compatibility—a gap in test scope, not a defect in v18 design intent, but a defect in deployment readiness.

next_action.rationale: Revert allocation rule set v18 to v17 to eliminate the split-reservation format that is incompatible with carrier protocol. This will prevent future orders from being allocated under v18 split-reservation rules. The action is reversible and idempotent, scoped to east-node reservation priority only. After revert, existing EXC-0921 held orders can be re-allocated under v17 rules via replay_held_allocations, which will generate single-node (non-split) reservations that carriers can process.
next_action.expected_information_gain: Mitigation: reverting v18 removes the root cause mechanism. Replaying held allocations will re-route orders to compatible (non-split) reservation patterns, enabling carrier pickup.
